title: List comprehensions
game_role: At the end of the game, your loot is valued with your filter.
objective: Build short, readable lists with list comprehensions and get to know lambda functions
story: In the corner of the workshop there's a magic mold: you throw materials in on one side and finished products come out the other. In Python this is called a **list comprehension**. It squeezes four-line loops into a single line!

sections.title: A list in one line
sections.body:
The long way to make a new list from a list:

```python
doubled = []
for n in nums:
    doubled.append(n * 2)
```

The short way with a list comprehension:

```python
doubled = [n * 2 for n in nums]
```

Read it like this: "for every n in nums, take n * 2."

sections.title: Picking with a condition
sections.body:
Add an `if` at the end to take only the items you want:

```python
big = [n for n in nums if n > 10]
evens = [n for n in range(20) if n % 2 == 0]
```

sections.title: Transforming with if and else
sections.body:
If you want to choose one of two results for each item, the `if ... else` goes **at the front**:

```python
labels = ["even" if n % 2 == 0 else "odd" for n in nums]
```

The same idea works for dictionaries and sets: `{n: n * n for n in range(4)}`

sections.title: lambda: a tiny nameless function
sections.body:
You can write small one-line functions with `lambda`:

```python
square = lambda x: x * x
print(square(5))   # 25

add = lambda a, b: a + b
```

`lambda` is especially handy with `sorted`, `map` and `filter`, which we'll see tomorrow.

examples.title: The long way, the short way
examples.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

doubled = []
for n in nums:
    doubled.append(n * 2)
print(doubled)

print([n * 2 for n in nums])

examples.title: Filter
examples.code:
scores = [45, 90, 12, 77, 100, 63]
passed = [s for s in scores if s >= 60]
print("Passed:", passed)
print(["pass" if s >= 60 else "fail" for s in scores])

examples.title: lambda
examples.code:
square = lambda x: x * x
add = lambda a, b: a + b
print(square(6))
print(add(2, 3))
print({n: square(n) for n in range(1, 5)})

tasks.title: Double it
tasks.prompt: Make a `doubled` list containing twice every number in `nums`, using a **list comprehension**.
tasks.solution:
nums = [3, 7, 10]

doubled = [n * 2 for n in nums]

print(doubled)
hints: The pattern: [expression for n in nums]

tasks.title: In capitals
tasks.prompt: Turn the names in `names` into capitals and put them in the `loud` list. Do it in one line.
tasks.solution:
names = ["piko", "emma", "ben"]

loud = [name.upper() for name in names]

print(loud)

tasks.title: Valuable loot
tasks.prompt: Take only the prices of 50 or more from `prices` and put them in the `valuable` list.
tasks.solution:
prices = [120, 5, 60, 49, 300, 1]

valuable = [p for p in prices if p >= 50]

print(valuable)
hints: Add an if at the end: [p for p in prices if ...]

challenge.title: With lambda
challenge.prompt: Write a **lambda** called `square` that returns the square of a number. Then the `squares` list should hold the squares of the numbers from 1 to `n`.
challenge.solution:
n = 5

square = lambda x: x * x

squares = [square(i) for i in range(1, n + 1)]

print(squares)
hints: range(1, n + 1) gives the numbers 1 to n.

project_task.title: Loot filter
project_task.prompt:
The items in Piko's bag are stored as `(name, value)` tuples. With one-line lists:

- `valuable`: the **names** of the items worth 50 or more
- `total`: the sum of all the items' values (you can use a list comprehension and `sum()`)
project_task.starter:
loot = [("sword", 120), ("rock", 1), ("potion", 60), ("rope", 8)]

valuable = []
total = 0

print("Valuable:", valuable)
print("Total value:", total)
project_task.solution:
loot = [("sword", 120), ("rock", 1), ("potion", 60), ("rope", 8)]

valuable = [name for name, price in loot if price >= 50]
total = sum([price for name, price in loot])

print("Valuable:", valuable)
print("Total value:", total)
hints: You can unpack tuples in the loop: for name, price in loot
total = sum([price for name, price in loot])
